mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: Returns remain positive when unemployment rises as specified.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate alongside low unemployment stimulates economic growth, boosting S&P 500 in 20 days.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between low FEDFUNDS, low UNRATE, and returns.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates in a tightening cycle lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are positive when FEDFUNDS exceed 4.5% in a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative despite industrial production growth.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when housing starts increase as specified.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales despite high federal funds rates indicate conflicting signals, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite conflicting signals.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth in a recovery regime leads to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: Returns are negative when payroll growth meets the trigger.
